subject: Sizing plan: Cortexica dedicated footprint & model memory floorplan
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Anna Liu <anna.liu@cortexica.ai>
Cc: Ben Soto <ben@cloudscale.io>
Date: 2027-05-12T16:14:00Z
Subject: Sizing plan: Cortexica dedicated footprint & model memory floorplan

Anna — great to meet yesterday. As discussed, Cortexica wants a committed Dedicated pool to run a POC followed by production for their clinical-document summarization product. Key asks:
- Support two model variants: a latency-optimized 13B and a quality 70B.
- Context targets: 4k typical; occasional 32k windows for long reports.
- Peak concurrency: planning for ~60 sustained QPS with 10% spiky headroom.
- Compliance: logs retained in VPC; customer will want SOC2 evidence (handled separately).

Marcus — can you provide a model-by-model memory floorplan (GPU RAM per replica), recommended pod counts for the committed throughput, and how int8/4-bit quantization will change the counts? Also include KV cache sizing and recommended headroom for canary rollouts.

I've included Ben from CloudScale to confirm if we should target A100-80GB or A100-40GB nodes for reserved capacity (they provide both in our region).

Next steps: Marcus to provide numbers and an initial capacity matrix; I'll use that to draft the reserved capacity commitment and price band to share with Procurement.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Anna Liu <anna.liu@cortexica.ai>
Cc: Ben Soto <ben@cloudscale.io>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-12T20:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Sizing plan: Cortexica dedicated footprint & model memory floorplan

Karthik / Anna — see attached capacity_matrix_v3.xlsx and kv_cache_profile.png for the worked numbers. Summary below (assumptions at bottom). TL;DR recommendations: reserve on A100-80GB where possible for the 70B variant; use A100-40GB for the 13B. Int8 quant reduces GPU memory pressure and increases per-GPU replicates by ~1.8x vs fp16; 4-bit (GPTQ-style) gives ~2.6x density but with an expected 6-8% quality hit on rare edge cases.

Model memory floorplan (per replica, runtime + KV cache):
- 13B (fp16, 4k context): 22 GB runtime + 6 GB KV cache = ~28 GB total -> fits on A100-40 (headroom required).
- 13B (int8, 4k context): 14 GB runtime + 4 GB KV cache = ~18 GB total -> fits comfortably, ~2 replicas per 40GB GPU estimated for production throughput.
- 13B (fp16, 32k context): 22 GB runtime + 48 GB KV cache (~1.5 GB per layer-avg * layers * tokens) = ~70 GB total -> requires A100-80 or offload strategy.
- 70B (fp16, 4k context): 38 GB runtime + 18 GB KV cache = ~56 GB total -> prefers A100-80GB.
- 70B (int8, 4k context): 24 GB runtime + 12 GB KV cache = ~36 GB total -> fits on A100-80 with good density.
- 70B (fp16, 32k context): 38 GB runtime + 192 GB KV cache = ~230 GB total -> not feasible on single GPU; requires split-KV serving (KV offload to host or remote KV store) or model sharding.

Throughput sizing (target: 60 sustained QPS, 10% spikes):
- 13B (primary, latency-sensitive path) using int8: recommend 12 replicas spread across 6x A100-40GB nodes (2 replicas per GPU) for baseline, add 2 GPUs as hot spare for spikes and canary.
- 70B (quality path) using int8: recommend 9 replicas on A100-80GB nodes (1 replica per GPU at lower concurrency due to longer token latency), target 9-12 GPUs depending on expected generation length; add 20% headroom for rollouts.

Quantization impact notes:
- Int8 reduces runtime memory by ~35-40% and KV footprint by ~20-30% (because activations quantize more aggressively).
- 4-bit (GPTQ) reduces runtime memory by ~55-65% and KV similarly, but requires extra dequant CPU ops; test on real prompts — quality regressions appear primarily on arithmetic and rare tokenization edge cases.

Operational recommendations:
- Default: commit to A100-80GB pool for the 70B plus mixed A100-40GB for 13B.
- Implement KV offload for any 32k+ windows (host memory or NVMe-backed cache). We can support transparent offload but expect increased tail latency during those requests.
- Canary rollout: keep 15-20% of capacity as reserve and use automatic fallback to smaller context or truncated prefix when kernel contention spikes.

Files attached: capacity_matrix_v3.xlsx (GPU-by-replica math), kv_cache_profile.png (token->KV bytes), se_runbook.txt (operational runbook).

Assumptions: model architecture similar to base LLMs with 1.5-2.0x KV multiplier per token depending on layer count; typical generation lengths for quality path ~800 tokens; P50 latency targets: 90ms (13B) / 450ms (70B) at baseline loads.

I'll add mitigation options for the 32k cases if Cortexica expects these windows regularly (paging/offload vs dynamic truncation).

—Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer, Inference Optimization
Redwood Inference
From: Anna Liu <anna.liu@cortexica.ai>

Date: 2027-05-13T09:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Sizing plan: Cortexica dedicated footprint & model memory floorplan

Thanks Marcus — this is super helpful and the attached matrix clarifies the trade-offs. A couple of clarifications from our side: 
- We expect ~70% of requests to be <=4k, ~20% at ~16k, and ~10% at or above 32k. The 32k requests come from bulk archive ingestion at night (non-latency critical).
- Our procurement team needs a simple SOW estimate (committed GPUs by month, expected monthly token throughput, and a high-level fallback/SLAs for the 32k fallback behavior).

Can you and Karthik produce a one-page SOW and an ops summary that calls out:
- Recommended committed pool (A100-80 vs A100-40 split)
- Expected monthly reserved GPU-hours for the POC (first 3 months) and steady-state
- Behavior for 32k windows (offload vs truncate) and expected latency delta when offloading

We prefer to start the POC using int8 for cost-efficiency; please note any known edge-cases we should validate during POC.

Anna Liu
Head of ML Systems
Cortexica Labs
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Anna Liu <anna.liu@cortexica.ai>
Cc: Ben Soto <ben@cloudscale.io>
Date: 2027-05-14T10:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Sizing plan: Cortexica dedicated footprint & model memory floorplan

Karthik / Marcus — quick internal note: I reviewed Marcus's matrix and agree with the conservative headroom for the 70B 32k scenario. For commercial framing on CRX-5821 we should:
- Propose a three-month POC with 8 A100-80GB + 6 A100-40GB reserved, int8 for initial run. That maps to the replica counts Marcus suggested with 15% buffer.
- For pricing, offer a 12% promotional discount on reserved capacity for the POC (to help close) and then standard tiered pricing for steady-state.
- Include an ops addendum that lists KV offload as an optional feature with expected latency delta: +200-800ms depending on context length and NVMe vs host RAM offload.

Karthik — if you can draft the one-page SOW using those numbers I will approve the discount and route to Finance. Marcus, please flag any must-test prompts for the POC validation (edge-cases where int8 may regress).

Thanks — LB
Lauren Bishop
Sales Manager, Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference
